summary: Sandoval County site on the Cuba Ranger District: a 1933 L-4 lookout house, replaced by a trailer per a 1989 survey; FFLA lists the site as gone.

facts.design: 14-foot-square wood-frame L-4 type lookout house, built 1933; a trailer lookout later
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the site as gone, with no date; the 1989 survey describes a trailer lookout on it
facts.agency: Santa Fe National Forest, Cuba Ranger District

events.note: 14-foot-square wood-frame L-4 type lookout house (survey text and figure caption)
The 1989 survey describes the trailer lookout and does not recommend it for National Register eligibility

evidence.supports: site listed in Sandoval County as a ground site, now gone
on the Cuba Ranger District of the Santa Fe National Forest; the trailer is the only trailer lookout in use on the forest in 1989
evidence.quote: Located on the Cuba Ranger District, the Red Top Lookout (Figure 242) is the only trailer lookout presently in use on the Santa Fe National Forest.

evidence.supports: lookout house built in 1933, 14 ft square wood frame, L-4 type; survey believes a trailer replaced it sometime in the 1960s
evidence.quote: It apparently replaced (sometime in the 1960s) a 14 feet square wood frame, L-4 type, lookout house built in 1933.

evidence.supports: the date the trailer was placed at the site is not known
evidence.quote: The date at which the lookout trailer was placed at the site is unknown.

evidence.supports: trailer not recommended for National Register eligibility
evidence.quote: This trailer lookout is not recommended

evidence.supports: photo caption: the house was constructed in 1933

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA codes the site as ground; the 1989 survey describes a trailer lookout on it. The 1933 house was a lookout house, and the survey believes a trailer replaced it sometime in the 1960s, so the two describe different structures at different times.

notes_for_editor: The 1989 USFS survey is the only source with a build date (1933) and the trailer. It gives no date for the trailer, only 'sometime in the 1960s', so no dated replaced event is recorded. The record's kind 'ground' fits the 1933 house; the trailer is a 'mobile' structure in Firefinder terms, so decide which structure the record should show. Status 'gone' comes from FFLA alone and is undated. No staffing, fire or access information was found; the Forest Lookouts Red Top page has only the agency. Two WebSearch calls were used; results for Red Top were mostly Washington and Idaho lookouts with the same name, which were not used.
